### workspace remove --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace remove [options] [NAME]

Delete a workspace's generated files: its tmuxinator config, its project
settings file and its state entry. Each file is copied aside first
(<file>.workspace-backup-<time>). The project's directory, git worktrees and
notes are never touched.

With no NAME, removes the workspace the current directory is in (a worktree's
marker, else an active workspace whose root holds it); not_in_workspace outside any.

Refuses while the workspace's tmux session is up (session_running; run
'workspace stop NAME' first) and for a worktree project (not_removable; use
'workspace kill', 'finish' or 'prune'). Asks before deleting unless --yes;
under --no-input it refuses without --yes.

Options:
        --name NAME                  The workspace to remove (default: the one detected from the current directory)
        --yes                        Skip the confirmation prompt
        --dry-run                    List what would be removed; no prompt, nothing changes
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes
                                     to stderr; a refusal is the error envelope. --json does not imply --yes: pass --yes in scripts

Examples:
  workspace remove myproject    # ask, then delete its tmuxinator config, settings file and state entry (backups kept; the checkout is untouched)
  workspace remove    # the same for the workspace you are in
  workspace remove myproject --dry-run    # see which files would go
  workspace remove myproject --yes --json    # no prompt, one action document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace remove --bogus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
invalid option: --bogus
--- end

### workspace remove
